title: Shared vs Private Egypt Tour: Real Cost Comparison for 1, 2 and 4 People
excerpt: How much does an Egypt private tour cost? Shared prices per person for Giza from €29, Luxor from €60 and Abu Simbel from €50, and what 1, 2 and 4 travellers pay.
body_html:
Prices, timetables and visiting details are a November 2026 snapshot. Check the linked official pages and your departure’s current inclusions and terms before booking.

Quick answer

A private tour in Egypt is priced per group: the vehicle, driver and guide are one cost shared among the travellers, so the private price per person falls as the group grows. Sawa's shared departures are priced per person instead, and the price does not move with headcount: Giza Uncovered from €29, Luxor in Depth from €75 and the Abu Simbel day from €50 per person, as listed in November 2026. For one or two travellers, shared is clearly the cheaper way to have a guide. At four, our cost estimate for a private Giza morning (about €28 each, before any operator margin) lands almost exactly on the €29 shared price, so ask for both.

Check current UK government travel advice for Egypt before making your arrangements; advice can change.

You have found two prices for the same Giza morning: €29 per person on a shared departure, and a private quote that changes with your headcount. Which number is really cheaper for a party of one, two or four? This post unpacks both pricing systems: how private tours are sold per vehicle, how Sawa Tours (sawa.tours), the Egypt shared-departure marketplace, sells seats per person instead, and what the listed prices for Giza, Luxor and Abu Simbel look like side by side. It focuses on the pricing mechanics; for the wider choice, see our guide to private, group and DIY touring.

What does an Egypt private tour cost?

There is no rate card: an Egypt private tour is quoted per group, not per person. The operator prices the vehicle, driver, fuel and licensed Egyptologist guide as one package, adds the entrance tickets, then divides the total by the travellers in it. One traveller carries the whole vehicle-and-guide cost; a couple splits it two ways; four split it four ways. That arithmetic is why a group discount is not generosity: the package cost barely moves while the number sharing it grows.

You can see the shape using the Giza Uncovered morning. This is our own estimate of what the day costs to run, not a private quote: the vehicle and driver at about EGP 1,850 and the guide at about EGP 2,000, so roughly EGP 3,850 is fixed whether one traveller turns up or eight; the plateau entrance ticket adds EGP 700 per traveller. At EGP 60 to the euro (8 November 2026):

Travellers Estimated cost to run the day Per person (estimate) Shared price per person
1 EGP 4,550 (about €76) About €76 €29
2 EGP 5,250 (about €88) About €44 €29
4 EGP 6,650 (about €111) About €28 €29

Read that table carefully, because it is a labelled estimate of the cost floor, not a quote. A private operator adds its own margin, may use a smaller or larger vehicle than a shared departure does, and may include things the shared day does not. What the floor shows is the direction and the scale. For a solo traveller, a private Giza morning costs well over twice the shared price before any margin. For a couple, the cost alone is about €15 a head above it. At four, the floor of about €28 sits almost exactly on the €29 shared price, so once a private operator adds its margin, a private quote for four will usually land at or a little above the shared price. That is why four is the headcount at which to ask for both.

Shared tour prices in Egypt: Sawa's prices for Giza, Luxor and Abu Simbel

Sawa's shared departures work in reverse: one tour on one date, filled with travellers pooled from several selling agencies, so the vehicle-and-guide cost is spread before you arrive. Sawa runs a fixed catalogue and sets the prices. The price is fixed per traveller and does not move with headcount. The figures below are per person, as listed in November 2026.

Tour (shared departure) Time From, per person 1 traveller 2 travellers 4 travellers
Giza Uncovered: Pyramids, Sphinx and Stories, from Cairo About 4 hrs €29 €29 €29 €29
Giza Pyramids, Sphinx and the Grand Egyptian Museum, from Cairo About 8 hrs €71 €71 €71 €71
The Grand West Bank: Tombs, Temples and Deir el-Medina, from Luxor About 9 hrs €60 €60 €60 €60
Luxor in Depth: East and West Bank, from Luxor About 9 hrs €75 €75 €75 €75
Aswan to Abu Simbel: Temples of Ramesses II and Nefertari About 9 hrs €50 €50 €50 €50

Compare inclusions, not just the headline. The four-hour Giza Uncovered tour includes the Giza plateau entrance ticket, the panorama and the Sphinx with a guide, but not entry inside the Great Pyramid, camel rides or meals. The eight-hour Giza Pyramids, Sphinx and Grand Egyptian Museum tour includes tickets for both sites plus lunch.

In Luxor, both full-day tours include a guide, transport, hotel pickup and entrance tickets. The Grand West Bank tour includes lunch; for Luxor in Depth, check the departure page. Special tombs are never included: Tutankhamun's (KV62) costs EGP 700 on top of the valley ticket, while Nefertari's (QV66) has been closed since March 2024. The Abu Simbel day tour includes hotel pickup in Aswan, the Abu Simbel tickets and lunch.

Private vs shared tour in Egypt: what you pay for 1, 2 and 4 people

Put the two systems side by side and the pattern is clear: the private per-person figure falls with every extra traveller, while the shared price stays where it started.

Travellers Private tour, per person Sawa shared departure, per person
1 Carries the whole vehicle-and-guide cost: on our Giza estimate, about €76 before margin The listed price: €29 for Giza Uncovered
2 The same package split two ways: about €44 each before margin Unchanged: €29 each; a couple pays exactly what a solo traveller pays
4 The same package split four ways: about €28 each before margin Still €29 each

Recommendation: for one or two travellers, the shared departure wins on price by a wide margin. At four, the two are roughly level on our estimate, so ask for both for the same itinerary and the same headcount, and compare what each includes. A confirmed Sawa date also cannot be cancelled for low numbers; private cancellation terms vary by operator, so ask what they are before you pay.

When a private tour in Egypt is worth the extra cost

Private tours buy control, not savings. They suit travellers who need a custom start time, families with young children, photographers chasing early light with nobody else in the frame, and anyone with mobility needs who wants the vehicle close all day (confirm access arrangements with the operator). If those needs are real, the premium is fair.

Sawa's start-your-own-date option narrows the gap: you pick any tour and day, Sawa's team reviews it, and other travellers can join, at the same fixed per-person price, never a private-tour quote.

When the shared departure is the better deal

Shared departures win for solo travellers (no solo surcharge on day tours, in a group of at most eight), for couples avoiding private prices, and for anyone whose last group tour was cancelled. The GoAhead rule addresses that failure: once a date has four travellers it is confirmed, and a confirmed date is not cancelled for low numbers.

Price certainty is the quiet advantage: the number on the departure page is the number you pay. On the nine-hour Luxor in Depth tour, every traveller on the date pays the same, from €75 per person, as listed in November 2026.

Five cost details most first-timers miss

  • The deposit is small. Nothing is charged at reservation. When a day-tour date confirms at four travellers you pay a 10% deposit, and the balance is due two days before departure, not full payment at booking.
  • Abu Simbel means a very early start. The temples sit about 280 km south of Aswan, 3.5 to 4 hours each way by road; the Abu Simbel day tour takes about 9 hours with hotel pickup in Aswan, tickets and lunch included (from €50, as listed in November 2026).
  • Special tombs always cost extra. Tutankhamun's tomb (KV62) is a separate ticket on every tour, shared or private. Nefertari's (QV66) has been closed since March 2024, so check before you build a day around it.
  • The €29 and €71 Giza tours are not the same day. One is four hours without lunch or interiors; the other is eight with tickets for the plateau and the museum, and lunch. Compare inclusions, then price.
  • Shared prices don't move with fill. Four travellers or eight, the per-person figure is identical. There is no group discount to wait for.

How to do this with Sawa Tours

Sawa Tours is a shared-departure marketplace, not a tour operator. Agencies sell the seats, and the departure is run by one of the licensed Egyptian agencies with travellers on the date, named before the deposit is due. Among the agencies on Sawa is a founding operating partner, Capital Travel Service (licence 2179).

Reserve a seat free on a forming date, with no card, or start your own. A date confirms when four travellers have reserved it, and a 10% deposit is then due by payment link, with the balance two days (48 hours) before departure. A forming date has until seven days before the tour to reach four; if it does not, it is cancelled, nothing is charged and we suggest another date. A traveller who does not pay after the GoAhead is excluded, and the tour still runs for the others. Cancel at least 48 hours before departure and you get a full refund; with less than 48 hours to go, the 10% deposit is retained. If force majeure (riots, a revolution and similar) stops the tour, you get a full refund. Groups never exceed eight travellers; when a date fills, a new independent departure opens. Payment is by a secure payment link from Online Era (General Sales Agent licence 32241); charges are in euros. Read the terms or browse the forming and confirmed departures.

The verdict: shared or private?

For one or two travellers, the shared departure is the clear money-saver: a fixed per-person price from €29 to €75 on the featured day tours, no solo surcharge, and nothing paid until four travellers have reserved the date. For a group of four, the two systems come out roughly level, about €28 against €29 on our Giza estimate, so request a private quote too and choose on what you value: a private tour's flexibility, or a shared date's fixed price and confirmed departure. faq.q: How much does a private tour in Egypt cost vs a group tour?
faq.a: A private tour is quoted per group: the vehicle, driver and guide form one cost divided among the travellers, so a solo traveller pays the most and a group of four roughly a quarter of the fixed part each. A shared departure is priced per person and does not move: from €29 for the four-hour Giza Uncovered tour to €75 for Luxor in Depth, as listed in November 2026. For one or two travellers, shared costs clearly less.

faq.q: Why is the per-person price the same for 1, 2 and 4 travellers on a Sawa departure?
faq.a: Because Sawa sets one price per traveller for each tour and pools travellers from several selling agencies onto the same date, so the fixed costs of the vehicle and guide are spread across the group rather than falling on whoever books first. There is no solo surcharge on day tours and no discount for a bigger group.

faq.q: Do solo travellers pay a surcharge on shared Egypt tours?
faq.a: Not on Sawa's day tours. The price is fixed per traveller with no solo surcharge: one person reserves at the same per-person price a couple pays. On cruises and packages with hotel nights, solo rooms and cabins are confirmed in the booking. That removes the single-supplement logic familiar from cruises and hotels, where a solo traveller pays for an empty place.

faq.q: Are entrance tickets included in Sawa's day-tour prices?
faq.a: Mostly, yes, but check each tour's inclusions list. Giza Uncovered includes the Giza plateau ticket but not entry inside the pyramids; the Giza and Grand Egyptian Museum, Luxor and Abu Simbel tours include their entrance tickets, and the Abu Simbel, Grand West Bank and Giza and museum tours include lunch (for Luxor in Depth, check the departure page). Special tombs such as Tutankhamun's (KV62) are separate tickets everywhere. Camel rides are never included.

faq.q: What happens if a shared departure never reaches four travellers?
faq.a: Nothing is charged. Reserving a seat is free, and no card is touched before the GoAhead. A date has until seven days before the tour to reach four; if it does not, it is cancelled, you pay nothing, and we suggest another date. Once confirmed, a date is not cancelled for low numbers.

faq.q: Is a private tour cheaper for a group of four?
faq.a: It can be close. On our Giza estimate, the cost of a private morning split four ways is about €28 each before any operator margin, against €29 shared, so a private quote for four will usually land at or slightly above the shared price. Ask for both quotes for the same itinerary. What a private booking cannot match is the mechanism: a shared departure keeps the same per-person price however the group fills, confirms at four with nothing paid before, and runs once confirmed.

faq.q: When do you actually pay for a Sawa shared departure?
faq.a: Not at reservation: holding a seat is free. When a day-tour date confirms at four travellers, you pay a 10% deposit by payment link; the balance is due two days before departure. Cancel at least 48 hours before departure and you get a full refund; with less than 48 hours to go, the 10% deposit is retained.
